American Brands -- EPS Up by 4%, But Tobacco Off by 16%
Inv. Code: Hold
Price: $32
April 22, 1993
American Brands's first quarter profits rose by 4% to $1.18 from $1.14 compared with a
10% decline we had been projecting due to non-operating factors including lower
corporate expense $5.0 million down from $22 million, other income of $5.7 million
versus other expense of $2.8 million and a 33.2% tax rate down from 35.5%. Full year
tax rate will equal 37% and would have cut first quarter profits by s0.07.
Operating profits declined 9% to $430.8 million while tobacco profits fell by 16% to
$267.6 million and non-tobacco eamings grew by 5% to $163.2 million or 37% of the
total.
We continue to code American Brands a Hold and believe the stock may react adversely
to the poor tobacco performance. We project lower earnings for the year - $3.65 down
by 12%, as American Brands starts to increase promotional activity. This compares with
a median IBES estimate of S4.18 with a range of $3.45-S4.81. The yield of 6.2% should
limit downside.
Domestic unit sales declined by 6.8%, but a 32% export gain limited the total unit
decline to 4.5%. Its full priced cigarettes fell by 14% but price value brands rose 2%.
Profits fell by 17% to $102.6 million on a 4.5% revenue gain to $407.5 million for a
25.1% pretax margin down from 31.6%.
We believe American Brands may discount half of its full priced cigarettes (about 17
billion cigarettes or 850 million packs) by $0.30 per pack This will burt profits by $128
million pretax, $83 million net For the full year we think domestic profits could drop by
29%. Discounting only one third of full priced cigarettes by $0.30 per pack would
produce a 20% drop and EPS of $3.80 per share.
Gallaher did well in sterling posting a 3% gain in sterting profits despite heavy
advertising for Benson & Hedges Super Kings, while dollar profits fell by 14% to $165.1
million as the value of the pound fell by 16% to $1.49 from $1.77. Gallaher shipments
rose by 6.9% due to pre-buying before a tax hike, while industry consumption fell by
6%. With exports, Gahllaher's unit volume grew by 11.4%.
Distilled spirit profits rose by 10% to 44.9 million on a 12% decline in sales to $246.6
million Jim Beam units grew by 14% in the U.S. and 9% woridwide. Worldwide branded
case sales grew 4%.
